The raised 2026 baseline revenue guidance of about US$10.3b and the new 2027 outlook around US$11.5b feed directly into that view.

data.title: Why LG Display Fell Even As It Turned A Profit
data.description:
LG Display just reported weaker revenue alongside a sharp swing back into profit, a result that would usually comfort long term investors rather than frustrate them. For LG Display shareholders, the loss over the past year was 47.1%, including dividends. If you had been weighing up a position in early November 2025, with bullish and cautious analysts split on OLED driven earnings power, what signals were actually visible before that outcome unfolded?

The easy part of this move is behind LG Display. Zero in on 227 high quality undervalued stocks for companies trading below our estimates.

The Two Stories LG Display Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost ₩14,050 at the start of the period, and investors were effectively choosing between two stories about where LG Display could reasonably end up.

The bullish narrative pointed to a Fair Value of ₩17,000, a price implied by assumptions that an OLED-centric mix, higher utilization, and tighter capital allocation would support revenue growth of 4.4% a year and a shift from a loss-making margin of 2.5% to a 7.1% profit margin by 2028.

The more cautious script anchored on a Fair Value of ₩12,195. In this scenario, analysts assumed revenue would edge down 0.6% a year, margins would only reach 4.8%, and heavy OLED capex plus competition from Chinese panel makers would keep pressure on earnings.

What The Results Changed For LG Display

The clearest new datapoint arrived in Q3 2026, when LG Display reported total revenue of ₩6,256,?35 million and net income of ₩755,635 million. Revenue fell against the prior year, while profit and net margin moved up from a small loss to 12.0%. That mix of weaker sales and stronger earnings cut both ways for the original bull and bear cases.

The main hinge here was profitability. When you assess another hardware-heavy group, compare any promised margin uplift with later reported net margin and cash generation, and not just with headline revenue hopes.

What LG Display’s Lower Price Asks You To Believe

LG Display trades at ₩7,090 today, after a 47.1% loss over the past year. The selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits above this level, based on a belief that an OLED heavy mix plus cost work can support sturdier earnings than the share price implies.

The argument leans on OLED accounting for most sales, growing auto display exposure, and production efficiency projects. For the fall to look like an opportunity rather than a warning, a buyer would need to believe OLED focused execution and restructuring can keep core operations profitable through patchy demand and currency swings.

"The main thing that has to go right is continued execution on OLED centric capacity use and cost innovation, including workforce restructuring and AI driven production efficiency, so that core operations stay profitable despite volatile demand and FX swings."

One Step Beyond LG Display

LG Display pulls you toward panels, pricing, and utilization. It is an obvious way to think about screens.

Your next question could be different. Who turns those screens and devices into a personal hub that people keep paying for?

One giant in consumer tech is betting on links between premium hardware, on device intelligence, and paid digital services.

It wants your phone, watch, headphones, and home gear to act together as a single assistant that learns, suggests, and sells.

If that model holds, the screens LG Display focuses on become just one entry point into a broader, subscription heavy ecosystem.

data.title: Keel Infrastructure (KEEL) Exits Bitcoin And Bets On AI Data Centers
data.description:
• Keel Infrastructure (NasdaqGM: KEEL) has sold its entire Bitcoin treasury and exited direct exposure to the cryptocurrency market.
  • The business is refocusing on building and leasing high-capacity data centers tailored to AI and high-performance computing workloads.
  • This change marks a material shift in Keel Infrastructure's long term plan away from cryptocurrency mining toward digital infrastructure services.
  • The pivot from Bitcoin holdings to AI and HPC data centers is important, but investors should weigh several other factors as well. Check out 3 warning signs (1 major) that Keel Infrastructure investors should know about.

For readers who want more ideas in this corner of the market, the next step is to compare peers through 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Keel Infrastructure runs digital and energy infrastructure that caters to high-performance computing and AI workloads across North America, which puts it squarely in the path of customers needing dense power, cooling, and reliable uptime for compute-heavy tasks. This positioning gives the business a clear operational link between this news and demand from AI and HPC clients.

1 thing going right for Keel Infrastructure that this headline doesn't cover.

How does selling the Bitcoin stack change Keel Infrastructure’s business model?

The shift takes Keel Infrastructure away from balance sheet exposure to Bitcoin prices and pushes it toward earning rent like income from AI and HPC tenants. Instead of holding 2,520 coins worth about US$192 million, the business is now leaning on its 2.2 GW development pipeline to drive future leasing. That moves risk from crypto volatility to construction, power and tenant demand.

Does this change the Keel Infrastructure Narrative?

The move lines up closely with the existing Narrative, which already framed Keel as an AI data center developer relying on long term leases and secured megawatts. Exiting Bitcoin holdings reinforces the catalyst around commercializing powered land at Panther Creek, Sharon and Moses Lake, while keeping the existing risks about funding costs and permitting delays firmly in play.

See how these catalysts shape Keel Infrastructure's path to a $6.14 fair value.

What should investors watch next to test whether this pivot is working?

The key proof point is signed, multi year leases on the new AI and HPC campuses, especially Moses Lake where construction has started and management has flagged 2027 as the first revenue year. Concrete metrics would be disclosed megawatts under contract, pricing per kilowatt and any update on cash runway as Q4 2026 and early 2027 results come through.
